cases.purpose: ntp query nts:HOST performs an RFC 8915 NTS-KE handshake with ALPN ntske/1 and sends the Next Protocol (NTPv4), AEAD (AES-SIV-CMAC-256) and End records. Limit: the candidate NTS-KE handshake fails against this independent OpenSSL TLS 1.3 peer (the published crypto nts-ke cases fail the same way), so later stages are unreached and the case FAILs.
cases.oracle: RFC 8915 (NTS-KE records, AES-SIV-CMAC-256 authenticator over [packet prefix, nonce], exporter label EXPORTER-network-time-security) and RFC 5905 header layout; an independent OpenSSL (ctypes) TLS 1.3 NTS-KE peer provides the exporter keys and python-cryptography AES-SIV checks every NTP packet.
cases.comparison: Candidate ntp query nts:127.0.0.1 inside a mapped user and mount namespace that bind-mounts the fixture CA over the system trust bundle (the NTS path passes no CA path); peer-side capture and the printed result are checked.
cases.setup_script:
mkfifo w.fifo
printf 'subjectAltName=DNS:trace.test,IP:127.0.0.1\nextendedKeyUsage=serverAuth\nbasicConstraints=critical,CA:FALSE\nkeyUsage=critical,digitalSignature,keyEncipherment\n' > "$HOME/server.ext"
/usr/bin/openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout "$HOME/ca.key" -out "$HOME/ca.pem" -days 1 -sha256 -subj '/CN=W2 Fixture CA' -addext 'basicConstraints=critical,CA:TRUE' -addext 'keyUsage=critical,keyCertSign,cRLSign' >/dev/null 2>&1
/usr/bin/openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout "$HOME/server.key" -out "$HOME/server.csr" -subj '/CN=trace.test' >/dev/null 2>&1
/usr/bin/openssl x509 -req -in "$HOME/server.csr" -CA "$HOME/ca.pem" -CAkey "$HOME/ca.key" -set_serial 2 -days 1 -sha256 -extfile "$HOME/server.ext" -out "$HOME/server.pem" >/dev/null 2>&1

files.q.sh:
t=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
[[ -e /etc/ssl/cert.pem ]] && t=/etc/ssl/cert.pem
/usr/bin/mount --bind "$HOME/ca.pem" "$t" || exit 90
ntp query nts:127.0.0.1 -t 5000

cases.script:
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w2-ntp-bash5320.py
exec 7<>w.fifo
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" serve good ready 2> serve.err &
srv=$!
for i in {1..100}; do [[ -e ready ]] && break; read -t 0.05 -u 7 l; done
/usr/bin/unshare --user --map-root-user --mount "$BASH" --noprofile --norc ./q.sh > query-out.txt 2> query-err.txt
echo "query-rc=$?"
read -t 0.3 -u 7 l
kill "$srv"; wait "$srv" 2>/dev/null
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" verify r1

cases.purpose: Negative paths (NTS-KE failure, no cookie, failed authenticator, wrong unique identifier) each give a nonzero status, no result line and the documented diagnostic.
